title: Illustrative: cooler walking routes to everyday services
summary: Fictional illustration: shaded routes and places to pause could make short summer journeys more manageable for older residents. All observations and findings in this record are invented for the demo.
strengthReason: Illustrative reviewer judgement: route observations and interviews align on comfort, but cannot establish changes in health or journey frequency.
methods: Fictional study: accompanied walks, shade mapping and repeat interviews during two warm-weather periods.
sampleContext: Fictional sample: 32 older residents using six invented neighbourhood routes; no actual streets or residents were studied.
findings: Illustrative finding: participants preferred routes combining shade with regular seating.
Illustrative finding: a shaded detour was less attractive when it added a difficult road crossing.
limitations: Illustrative limitation: volunteers were already able to walk outdoors.
Illustrative limitation: short observation periods cannot describe seasonal effects.
useNotes: Illustrative use: discuss shade, seating and crossings together when scoping a route audit.
Illustrative caution: do not treat these invented findings as an estimate of heat-related health benefits.

title: Illustrative: opening shared courtyards for everyday use
summary: Fictional illustration: a courtyard-access pilot explores whether opening hours, lighting and clear responsibilities support use of shared outdoor space. This is invented evaluation content, not a real local finding.
strengthReason: Illustrative reviewer judgement: recorded use increased in two settings but not the third; weather and concurrent activities offer alternative explanations.
methods: Fictional evaluation: before-and-after observation logs and resident interviews without a comparison group.
sampleContext: Fictional sample: three invented housing courtyards and 45 interview participants over twelve weeks.
findings: Illustrative finding: predictable opening times helped residents plan short visits.
Illustrative finding: uncertainty about who could enter persisted where signage was unclear.
limitations: Illustrative limitation: observations overlapped with improving weather.
Illustrative limitation: people avoiding the courtyards were underrepresented.
useNotes: Illustrative use: include access rules and maintenance ownership in a pilot checklist.

title: Illustrative: resident accounts of evening street comfort
summary: Fictional illustration: residents describe how lighting, sightlines and the presence of other people shape comfort on evening journeys. These community accounts are invented and do not describe actual local conditions.
strengthReason: Illustrative reviewer judgement: recurring accounts across three discussion formats support a consistent experiential theme, not an estimate of crime or safety outcomes.
methods: Fictional engagement: evening walk-alongs, annotated maps and separate discussions with shift workers.
sampleContext: Fictional sample: 54 residents discussing four invented walking corridors.
findings: Illustrative finding: reliable lighting mattered more to participants than very bright isolated spots.
Illustrative finding: active frontages offered reassurance, while busy traffic could still deter walking.
limitations: Illustrative limitation: reported comfort is not a measure of recorded harm.
Illustrative limitation: recruitment through local activities missed some isolated residents.
useNotes: Illustrative use: combine resident walk-alongs with accessibility audits before designing changes.

title: Illustrative: crossings and family school journeys
summary: Fictional illustration: a school-journey study considers how crossing delays and accompanying younger siblings influence walking choices. Every sample and finding is illustrative rather than a real study result.
strengthReason: Illustrative reviewer judgement: journey diaries and observed crossing delays support the same narrow access finding, without proving a health effect.
methods: Fictional study: two-week journey diaries paired with structured crossing observations and caregiver interviews.
sampleContext: Fictional sample: 80 households travelling to four invented schools across two area contexts.
findings: Illustrative finding: unpredictable waits complicated journeys with multiple children.
Illustrative finding: families valued continuous accessible routes over isolated improvements near the school gate.
limitations: Illustrative limitation: participating households may be more interested in walking than nonparticipants.
Illustrative limitation: travel patterns outside term time were not examined.
useNotes: Illustrative use: assess complete household journeys when framing a school-access project.

title: Illustrative: timing of family food sessions
summary: Fictional illustration: an evaluation explores whether session times and childcare arrangements affect access to a family cooking offer. The service, participants and results are entirely invented.
strengthReason: Illustrative reviewer judgement: attendance patterns differ by session time and household circumstances, with insufficient evidence about sustained dietary change.
methods: Fictional evaluation: attendance analysis, exit conversations and follow-up calls six weeks after sessions.
sampleContext: Fictional sample: 65 households offered sessions at two invented community venues.
findings: Illustrative finding: later sessions suited some working carers but conflicted with bedtime routines for others.
Illustrative finding: participants described childcare as important to repeat attendance.
limitations: Illustrative limitation: follow-up was incomplete among households attending only once.
Illustrative limitation: food intake was not independently measured.
useNotes: Illustrative use: test a choice of session times rather than assuming one schedule fits all families.

title: Illustrative: young people's accounts of belonging
summary: Fictional illustration: young people discuss welcoming spaces, adult relationships and the cost of participation. These invented accounts are prompts for discussion, not evidence about actual young people or services.
strengthReason: Illustrative reviewer judgement: detailed accounts offer useful questions, but a small, connected participant group limits breadth of perspectives.
methods: Fictional engagement: participant-led photo prompts and two facilitated group conversations.
sampleContext: Fictional sample: 14 young people recruited through one invented after-school activity.
findings: Illustrative finding: participants valued being recognised by a trusted adult without having to book in advance.
Illustrative finding: small transport and activity costs could accumulate across a week.
limitations: Illustrative limitation: young people outside organised activities were not represented.
Illustrative limitation: group settings may discourage disagreement.
useNotes: Illustrative use: use these themes to design broader listening, not to generalise preferences to all young people.

title: Illustrative: supported handovers for carers
summary: Fictional illustration: practitioners document a small trial of supported handovers between family advice offers. The workflow and learning are invented for the demo and make no claim about real services.
strengthReason: Illustrative reviewer judgement: reflective logs identify plausible workflow issues but lack independent follow-up and a comparison process.
methods: Fictional practice learning: weekly reflective logs and a review of anonymised example referral journeys.
sampleContext: Fictional sample: eight practitioners and 22 invented referral journeys over six weeks.
findings: Illustrative finding: agreeing a contact time reduced repeated attempts to reach carers.
Illustrative finding: handover tasks became unclear when the receiving service was unavailable.
limitations: Illustrative limitation: accounts come primarily from practitioners rather than carers.
Illustrative limitation: completed contact does not establish whether support met a household's needs.
useNotes: Illustrative use: specify responsibility and consent at each handover step before piloting.

title: Illustrative: predictable shift notice and household routines
summary: Fictional illustration: a study explores relationships between shift-notice periods, care arrangements and reported stress. All employers, participants and findings are invented; no real organisation is represented.
strengthReason: Illustrative reviewer judgement: survey and interview patterns broadly align, but income and job security may confound the reported associations.
methods: Fictional study: cross-sectional survey and follow-up interviews about weekly scheduling.
sampleContext: Fictional sample: 210 workers in invented retail, hospitality and care settings.
findings: Illustrative finding: shorter notice was associated with more reported changes to childcare plans.
Illustrative finding: workers with predictable hours still described stress when total paid hours varied.
limitations: Illustrative limitation: cross-sectional data cannot establish causation.
Illustrative limitation: self-reported schedules were not checked against payroll records.
useNotes: Illustrative use: distinguish notice, hours and pay when developing questions about secure work.

title: Illustrative: income advice at neighbourhood drop-ins
summary: Fictional illustration: a pilot tests access to income advice through familiar drop-in settings. The service and outcomes are fabricated solely as clearly labelled demo material.
strengthReason: Illustrative reviewer judgement: appointment logs and participant follow-up consistently describe easier initial access; longer-term income effects remain unassessed.
methods: Fictional evaluation: appointment monitoring and structured follow-up interviews after first contact.
sampleContext: Fictional sample: 96 advice contacts across three invented drop-in venues over four months.
findings: Illustrative finding: being able to ask a brief question before booking reduced uncertainty about eligibility.
Illustrative finding: private space was important when discussing debt or household circumstances.
limitations: Illustrative limitation: people who never approached a drop-in were not interviewed.
Illustrative limitation: repeat contacts were not evidence of resolved financial problems.
useNotes: Illustrative use: include privacy and onward appointment capacity in an access pilot.

title: Illustrative: workers' accounts of places to rest
summary: Fictional illustration: mobile workers discuss finding toilets, drinking water and places to pause between tasks. These invented community accounts do not report conditions at any real workplace.
strengthReason: Illustrative reviewer judgement: accounts agree on the importance of basic facilities but differ by work pattern and ability to take breaks.
methods: Fictional engagement: audio diaries and small-group mapping of typical working days.
sampleContext: Fictional sample: 26 mobile workers in invented delivery and home-visit roles.
findings: Illustrative finding: a facility's opening times could matter as much as its distance from a route.
Illustrative finding: unpaid waiting and tight schedules limited use of otherwise available rest spaces.
limitations: Illustrative limitation: participation required time away from paid work.
Illustrative limitation: the accounts do not measure occupational health outcomes.
useNotes: Illustrative use: consider employment conditions alongside the physical availability of facilities.

title: Illustrative: ventilation, noise and indoor air
summary: Fictional illustration: an indoor-air study examines how noise, security and heating costs shape ventilation choices. All measurements and households are invented; this is not evidence about actual housing conditions.
strengthReason: Illustrative reviewer judgement: monitoring and diaries indicate several interacting barriers, with substantial variation between homes and no intervention comparison.
methods: Fictional study: short-term indoor monitoring paired with household ventilation diaries and interviews.
sampleContext: Fictional sample: 28 invented homes with differing layouts, occupancy patterns and road exposure.
findings: Illustrative finding: some households avoided opening windows during noisy periods.
Illustrative finding: advice to ventilate was harder to follow when residents were concerned about heat loss or security.
limitations: Illustrative limitation: brief monitoring cannot represent annual exposure.
Illustrative limitation: sensors were not used to diagnose individual health conditions.
useNotes: Illustrative use: pair ventilation discussions with assessment of practical housing constraints.
Illustrative caution: this invented record is not technical or clinical advice.

title: Illustrative: a school-gate traffic and air pilot
summary: Fictional illustration: an evaluation considers a timed vehicle-access pilot near invented schools. Monitoring patterns and family experiences are illustrative and must not be attributed to real schools or local programmes.
strengthReason: Illustrative reviewer judgement: a brief monitoring window and changing weather prevent confident attribution of air-quality differences to the pilot.
methods: Fictional evaluation: traffic counts, portable air monitoring and caregiver feedback before and during a pilot.
sampleContext: Fictional sample: two invented school entrances monitored for ten school days each.
findings: Illustrative finding: fewer vehicles were observed at the restricted entrance during operating times.
Illustrative finding: monitoring results varied across days and could not isolate the pilot's contribution.
limitations: Illustrative limitation: nearby displacement streets were monitored incompletely.
Illustrative limitation: no respiratory health outcomes were measured.
useNotes: Illustrative use: plan comparison locations, weather adjustment and access exemptions before a larger evaluation.

title: Illustrative: a hot-weather check-in workflow
summary: Fictional illustration: a practice team reflects on arranging hot-weather check-ins with older people. The workflow, contacts and learning are invented and are not a real emergency-response evaluation.
strengthReason: Illustrative reviewer judgement: repeated workflow reviews consistently identify the same contact-management issue; this judgement applies only to process learning.
methods: Fictional practice learning: structured debriefs and contact-log reviews across three simulated hot-weather periods.
sampleContext: Fictional sample: twelve staff and volunteers using 40 invented participant contact plans.
findings: Illustrative finding: an agreed preferred contact method reduced duplicate attempts.
Illustrative finding: unclear escalation ownership created delays when a participant could not be reached.
limitations: Illustrative limitation: simulations cannot establish performance during an actual emergency.
Illustrative limitation: no heat-related health outcomes were assessed.
useNotes: Illustrative use: explore contact preferences and escalation ownership when reviewing a workflow.
Illustrative caution: this record is not a heat-health protocol.

title: Illustrative: rental costs and household wellbeing review
summary: Fictional illustration: an invented evidence review explores links between housing costs, financial strain and wellbeing in urban contexts. It cites no real studies and reports no real synthesis findings.
strengthReason: Illustrative reviewer judgement: the imagined studies use differing affordability measures and largely observational designs, limiting a shared interpretation.
methods: Fictional review: structured comparison of invented study summaries using a predefined extraction template.
sampleContext: Fictional sample: twelve invented urban study summaries; no actual publications were reviewed.
findings: Illustrative finding: residual income after housing costs captured different pressures from rent-to-income ratios.
Illustrative finding: moving costs and housing insecurity were often intertwined with affordability.
limitations: Illustrative limitation: differing measures prevent meaningful pooled estimates.
Illustrative limitation: wider-context mechanisms may not transfer directly to either area.
useNotes: Illustrative use: specify an affordability definition before comparing future real sources.

title: Illustrative: flexible childcare booking for variable hours
summary: Fictional illustration: a small booking pilot considers the needs of carers working variable hours. The offer and its results are invented, with no claim about existing childcare providers.
strengthReason: Illustrative reviewer judgement: a small self-selecting pilot offers early access learning but cannot demonstrate effects on employment or child wellbeing.
methods: Fictional evaluation: booking records, cancellation logs and interviews with participating carers.
sampleContext: Fictional sample: 24 households using one invented flexible-hours childcare offer over eight weeks.
findings: Illustrative finding: shorter booking lead times were helpful when work schedules changed.
Illustrative finding: limited late-afternoon capacity still left gaps for some households.
limitations: Illustrative limitation: the pilot did not include households unable to afford the offer.
Illustrative limitation: provider staffing costs were not fully assessed.
useNotes: Illustrative use: evaluate affordability and provider feasibility alongside booking flexibility.

title: Illustrative: resident diaries of repair access
summary: Fictional illustration: residents keep diaries about requesting repairs and arranging access to their homes. These experiences are invented and do not describe any real landlord, building or repair service.
strengthReason: Illustrative reviewer judgement: repeated communication themes emerge, while differing repair complexity makes completion experiences difficult to compare.
methods: Fictional engagement: six-week resident diaries with individual follow-up conversations.
sampleContext: Fictional sample: 31 households describing invented repair requests in varied housing settings.
findings: Illustrative finding: clear updates reduced uncertainty even when repair completion took time.
Illustrative finding: broad appointment windows disrupted work and caring routines.
limitations: Illustrative limitation: diary entries were not matched to service records.
Illustrative limitation: the sample cannot estimate the prevalence of repair problems.
useNotes: Illustrative use: include communication and appointment burden in a resident-experience framework.

title: Illustrative: summer comfort in small urban homes
summary: Fictional illustration: a wider-context study explores how home layout and daily routines influence reported summer comfort. Its observations and results are invented and cannot support local prevalence estimates.
strengthReason: Illustrative reviewer judgement: repeated diary and temperature patterns align within the imagined sample, but do not establish intervention effectiveness or wider prevalence.
methods: Fictional study: room-temperature logging and comfort diaries across two summer periods.
sampleContext: Fictional sample: 48 invented small urban homes outside a specified area context.
findings: Illustrative finding: homes with limited options for night-time ventilation retained warmth longer.
Illustrative finding: residents spending more time at home described fewer opportunities to avoid uncomfortable rooms.
limitations: Illustrative limitation: the invented sample does not represent all building types.
Illustrative limitation: comfort ratings are not diagnoses of heat-related illness.
useNotes: Illustrative use: frame questions about occupancy and ventilation when planning future local research.

title: Illustrative: choosing family appointment reminders
summary: Fictional illustration: a practice team tests a conversation about preferred reminder channels for family appointments. All contacts and learning are invented; no real service performance is described.
strengthReason: Illustrative reviewer judgement: reflective logs describe easier contact for some carers but persistent barriers for those sharing devices or changing numbers.
methods: Fictional practice learning: short improvement cycles using staff logs and optional carer feedback.
sampleContext: Fictional sample: 36 invented appointment journeys across two imaginary family support teams.
findings: Illustrative finding: asking about channel and timing preferences surfaced otherwise hidden contact barriers.
Illustrative finding: digital reminders alone did not resolve difficulties caused by unpredictable schedules.
limitations: Illustrative limitation: feedback was voluntary and mostly from carers reached successfully.
Illustrative limitation: no comparison group or long-term attendance analysis was available.
useNotes: Illustrative use: revisit contact preferences and offer a non-digital route when designing reminders.

title: Illustrative: unreleased register validation fixture
summary: Fictional illustration: UNRELEASED_FIXTURE_SENTINEL is an invented test-only record used to verify release filtering. It must never appear in public catalogue output, routes or browser assets.
strengthReason: Illustrative reviewer judgement: this invented fixture has no evidential value and exists only to exercise validation and release controls.
methods: Fictional fixture method: a synthetic practice-learning entry for automated checks.
sampleContext: Fictional fixture context: no actual participants, services or organisations.
findings: Illustrative fixture finding: release approval is required before publication.
limitations: Illustrative fixture limitation: this is test data, not substantive evidence.
useNotes: Illustrative fixture use: build-time release-filter tests only.
